judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 1919, the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, which barred the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency or holding accounts for individuals, and from studying or testing one without authorization from Congress. It passed the House 219-210.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 1919, the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, which barred the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency or holding accounts for individuals, and from studying or testing one without authorization from Congress. It passed the House 219-210.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.J.Res. 104, which used the Congressional Review Act to repeal the Bureau of Land Management plan for the Miles City field office in eastern Montana, reopening those federal lands to coal leasing. It passed the House 211-208.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.J.Res. 104, which used the Congressional Review Act to repeal the Bureau of Land Management plan for the Miles City field office in eastern Montana, reopening those federal lands to coal leasing. It passed the House 211-208.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.J.Res. 106, which used the Congressional Review Act to repeal the Bureau of Land Management plan for Alaska's Central Yukon area, undoing its designation of areas of critical environmental concern. It passed the House 215-210.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.J.Res. 106, which used the Congressional Review Act to repeal the Bureau of Land Management plan for Alaska's Central Yukon area, undoing its designation of areas of critical environmental concern. It passed the House 215-210.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.J.Res. 105, which used the Congressional Review Act to repeal the Bureau of Land Management plan for the North Dakota field office that had limited oil and gas development in low-potential areas and narrowed new coal leasing. It passed the House 215-211.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.J.Res. 105, which used the Congressional Review Act to repeal the Bureau of Land Management plan for the North Dakota field office that had limited oil and gas development in low-potential areas and narrowed new coal leasing. It passed the House 215-211.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 3838, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, which set defense policy and authorized spending for Department of Defense programs, military construction, and the Energy Department's national security programs. It passed the House 231-196.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 3838, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, which set defense policy and authorized spending for Department of Defense programs, military construction, and the Energy Department's national security programs. It passed the House 231-196.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 3486, the Stop Illegal Entry Act, which set a five-year mandatory minimum sentence, and allowed a life sentence, for immigrants who enter the country illegally and are later convicted of a felony or who reenter after removal. It passed the House 226-197.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 3486, the Stop Illegal Entry Act, which set a five-year mandatory minimum sentence, and allowed a life sentence, for immigrants who enter the country illegally and are later convicted of a felony or who reenter after removal. It passed the House 226-197.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 4922, the DC CRIMES Act, which stripped the District of Columbia of authority to change criminal sentences and lowered the maximum age for youth offender sentencing from 24 to 18. It passed the House 240-179.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 4922, the DC CRIMES Act, which stripped the District of Columbia of authority to change criminal sentences and lowered the maximum age for youth offender sentencing from 24 to 18. It passed the House 240-179.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.R. 5140, which lowered the age at which a minor can be tried as an adult in the District of Columbia for certain serious offenses from 16 to 14. It passed the House 225-203.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against passing H.R. 5140, which lowered the age at which a minor can be tried as an adult in the District of Columbia for certain serious offenses from 16 to 14. It passed the House 225-203.
